cohort: The study included nulliparous women delivering singleton neonates in cephalic presentation weighting 2,500 to 4,000g.
finding: Infants born by vacuum extraction have significantly higher rates of intracranial haemorrhage than those born by spontaneous vaginal delivery, although the absolute risk is small.
mod_finding: Vacuum extraction was associated with significantly higher rates of intracranial haemorrhage compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery, with no significant differences found between vacuum extraction and emergency caesarean delivery.
